description: This topic deals with the physical combination of two or more ingredients and calculating their optimum mixing ratio. Alligation is a mathematical technique used to quickly determine the average price of mixed quantities or the exact ratio in which ingredients of different prices must be combined to achieve a desired average price.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Key terms and definitions related to the concepts of Mixtures and Alligations.

key_concepts.explanation: A physical combination of two or more substances or ingredients to produce a final compound.
The ingredient used in the mixture that has a lower cost per unit.
The ingredient used in the mixture that has a higher cost per unit.
The cost per unit of the resultant mixture, which always lies between the price of the cheaper (c) and dearer (d) ingredients.

sections.title: Rule of Alligation
sections.description: This rule is applied to find the exact ratio in which two ingredients of different prices must be mixed to obtain a mixture of a desired mean price.

equations: (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (d - m) / (m - c)

key_concepts.explanation: The ratio of the quantity of the cheaper ingredient to the quantity of the dearer ingredient is always equal to (d - m) : (m - c).

sections.title: Repeated Replacement or Dilution
sections.description: This concept is applied when a certain quantity is withdrawn from a pure liquid and replaced with another liquid (like water), and this process is repeated multiple times.

key_concepts.explanation: Here 'x' represents the initial quantity of the pure liquid, 'y' is the quantity replaced in each operation, and 'n' is the total number of replacement operations performed.

sections.title: Problem Solving Steps
sections.description: A systematic method to solve questions using the Alligation Cross Diagram.

steps.title: Identify the Values
steps.detail: Clearly extract the price of the cheaper ingredient (c), the dearer ingredient (d), and the desired mean price (m) from the problem statement.

steps.title: Ensure Uniform Units
steps.detail: Verify that c, d, and m are in the same unit (e.g., all must be Cost Price). If the Selling Price of the mixture is given, convert it to Cost Price first.

steps.title: Cross Subtraction
steps.detail: Draw the alligation cross diagram. Subtract the mean price from the dearer price (d - m) and subtract the cheaper price from the mean price (m - c) diagonally.

steps.title: Calculate Ratio
steps.detail: The resulting values give the ratio (d - m) : (m - c). This is the required ratio in which the quantities must be mixed.
